ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the gingiva

facts.raw_span: A 69-year-old Japanese man presented with pain and a 10-mm polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva
He had undergone chemoradiotherapy 15 years earlier for squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa, with no recurrence until now
He denied tobacco or alcohol use
trismus was present
a rough-surfaced polypoid lesion in the left lower molar gingiva covered by a whitish pseudomembrane
Panoramic radiography showed a moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption
Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated an enhancing soft-tissue mass with irregular mandibular bone destruction
A biopsy specimen showed loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells in a fibrin-rich edematous stroma alongside inflammatory cells
The spindle cells had basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses; many contained neutrophils within cytoplasmic vacuoles
Immunohistochemical staining revealed that the spindle cells were positive for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, p63, p53, and CD68, but negative for pan-cytokeratin and other epithelial markers
Ki-67 labeling index was approximately 50%
These findings prompted consideration of a malignant spindle cell process

concepts.preferred_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the gingiva
concepts.why: The patient has a history of squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa and presents with a new polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva, suggesting a possible recurrence or new primary tumor.
The biopsy specimen shows atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells with basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses, which are characteristic features of malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
The spindle cells are positive for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, and p63, which are markers of smooth muscle differentiation, suggesting a possible diagnosis of leiomyosarcoma.
The patient presents with trismus and a rough-surfaced polypoid lesion, which could be consistent with an inflammatory pseudotumor.
The patient has a history of trauma to the left lower gingiva and presents with a polypoid mass, which could be consistent with a diagnosis of gingival fibromatosis.

The patient has a history of squamous cell carcinoma and presents with a new tumor that shows both epithelial and mesenchymal differentiation, suggesting a possible diagnosis of sarcomatoid carcinoma.
The patient presents with a polypoid mass and trismus, which could be consistent with a diagnosis of giant cell granuloma.
The patient presents with a moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption and an enhancing soft-tissue mass, which could be consistent with a diagnosis of osteosarcoma of the mandible.

rationales.F01: Polypoid mass on the gingiva is a common presentation for several conditions, including squamous cell carcinoma and malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
rationales.F02: History of squamous cell carcinoma increases the likelihood of recurrence or development of a new primary tumor, such as sarcomatoid carcinoma.
rationales.F06: Moth-eaten pattern of bone resorption is suggestive of an aggressive process, such as osteosarcoma or malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
rationales.F07: Enhancing soft-tissue mass with bone destruction is consistent with several malignant conditions, including osteosarcoma and sarcomatoid carcinoma.
rationales.F08: Presence of atypical spindle cells is indicative of a malignant process, such as malignant fibrous histiocytoma or leiomyosarcoma.
rationales.F09: Spindle cells with basophilic cytoplasm and atypical mitoses are characteristic of malignant fibrous histiocytoma or leiomyosarcoma.
rationales.F10: Immunohistochemical staining pattern is consistent with malignant fibrous histiocytoma or leiomyosarcoma, and rules out squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F11: High Ki-67 labeling index indicates a high proliferative rate, consistent with a malignant process such as malignant fibrous histiocytoma or leiomyosarcoma.
rationales.F12: Consideration of a malignant spindle cell process is based on the combination of clinical, radiologic, and histopathologic findings.

high Ki-67 labeling index is not typical of squamous cell carcinoma
